themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked to 129 THIS WEEK—a 514% jump from the 21-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 10.99)—signaling a widespread infrastructure failure or weather event impact in Far Rockaway that demands immediate public works assessment.
evidence: 129 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 21.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 10.99)
Curb condition complaints up 1100% THIS WEEK (3 complaints vs. 0.2 avg, z-score: 6.35)
Damaged tree complaints up 336% THIS WEEK (6 complaints vs. 1.4 avg, z-score: 6.65)
reporting_angles: Ground-truth reporting: photograph the streets and curbs residents are complaining about; identify specific blocks with highest complaint density
Accountability angle: what triggered this spike—recent storm damage, deferred maintenance, or under-resourced street crews in a waterfront district?

themes_detail.label: Street Sweeping Neglect
themes_detail.summary: Street sweeping complaints exploded to 6 LAST WEEK—a 1500% increase from the 0.4 weekly baseline (z-score: 11.62, the highest-severity spike in the dataset)—suggesting sanitation crews are not servicing neighborhoods regularly, compounding broader infrastructure complaints.
evidence: 6 street sweeping complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 11.62, highest severity spike)
Overlaps with spike in street condition (129 complaints THIS WEEK), suggesting debris/dirt is degrading street quality
Residential disposal complaints also up 371% LAST WEEK (10 vs. 2.1 avg, z-score: 6.21), indicating sanitation system under stress
reporting_angles: Service gap: interview Sanitation Department about street sweeping schedules in CD414 and any crew shortages or route changes
Resident impact: find neighbors with photos of unsanitary streets; connect to broader maintenance failures reported THIS WEEK

themes_detail.label: Residential Plumbing Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Plumbing complaints jumped to 3 LAST WEEK—a 300% spike from the 0.8 weekly average (z-score: 5.2)—while heat/hot water remains the top complaint category (1510 over 90 days), indicating a potential systemic issue with building water systems in aging Far Rockaway housing stock.
evidence: Plumbing complaints up 300% LAST WEEK (3 vs. 0.8 avg, z-score: 5.2)
Heat/hot water is #1 complaint category overall (1510 complaints over 90 days), suggesting water system infrastructure failure is chronic
Water system complaints also elevated at 301 over 90-day period, ranking 9th by volume
reporting_angles: Systemic aging: investigate the age of building stock, boiler systems, and plumbing in Far Rockaway; connect to DOE/DEP capital budget requests for infrastructure
Tenant vulnerability: identify vulnerable populations (elderly, low-income renters) affected by winter heating/water failures; contact tenant advocacy groups

themes_detail.label: Tree Maintenance Backlog
themes_detail.summary: Damaged tree complaints spiked to 6 THIS WEEK (336% above the 1.4 weekly average, z-score: 6.65), while overgrown tree/branch complaints were elevated 3 WEEKS AGO (5 complaints, 471% spike, z-score: 5.28), suggesting inadequate Parks Department tree trimming and storm response in CD414.
evidence: Damaged tree complaints up 336% THIS WEEK (6 vs. 1.4 avg, z-score: 6.65)
Overgrown tree/branch complaints spiked 3 WEEKS AGO (5 vs. 0.9 avg, z-score: 5.28), indicating sustained maintenance deficit
Both spikes suggest weather event or systematic Parks Department neglect in waterfront district vulnerable to storms
reporting_angles: Parks response: request data from Parks Department on tree trimming schedules, storm damage assessments, and budget for Far Rockaway
Resident safety: document instances where fallen branches or damaged trees pose hazards to homes or streets; connect to broader infrastructure neglect story

themes_detail.label: Wayfinding Infrastructure Gaps
themes_detail.summary: Street sign complaints spiked to 5 THREE WEEKS AGO—a 700% jump from the 0.6 weekly baseline (z-score: 5.11)—indicating navigation and municipal infrastructure deficits that may compound resident frustration during transit and service interactions.
evidence: Street sign missing complaints up 700% 3 WEEKS AGO (5 vs. 0.6 avg, z-score: 5.11)
Spike is older than street/curb/tree spikes THIS WEEK but still elevated, suggesting persistent municipal maintenance neglect
Overlaps with broader pattern of street infrastructure failures and deferred maintenance across district
reporting_angles: Audit: walk key pedestrian corridors in Far Rockaway with a visual checklist of missing/damaged street signs; photograph gaps
Systemic negligence: connect missing street signs to broader street condition crisis and Parks/DOT under-resourcing in outer-borough district
